followup_questions.purpose: Encourage creative problem-solving and broader context

reasoning_path: Initial claim about short videos → Mechanism of content length → Evidence requirement → Boundary conditions (counterexamples) → Causal analysis → Comparative generalization

misconception_flags.misconception: Students often assume ‘shorter content’ automatically translates to ‘better learning outcomes’ without considering attention limits, content depth, subject matter complexity, or individual learning differences

teacher_guidance: Start with Q1 to probe the assumed mechanism. If the student struggles to articulate why shorter content helps, pause and provide a concrete example about attention vs. depth trade-offs before proceeding to Q2 on evidence. Question Q3 should be used to surface hidden assumptions about universal effectiveness.
